requirements.requirement: Convert the staged Latin-1 filenames into UTF-8 filenames under converted/, retaining directory structure and file contents.
requirements.summary: The UTF-8 byte sequences for café.txt and résumé.txt are directly observed under converted/, and each destination hash matches its corresponding Latin-1-named source. The staged tree is flat, so no deeper directory hierarchy required demonstration. The same state remained healthy after restart.
All three imported files remain present with their original filename bytes. Their final hashes match the preparation baseline, including plain.txt and both Latin-1-named files.

requirements.summary: The existing converted/plain.txt collision was recorded in migration-report.txt. Direct hash checks show both the source and pre-existing destination retained their distinct baseline contents, including after restart.

requirements.requirement: Keep the installed operating-system release and kernel, using software compatible with the legacy platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution, node1 remained Alpine Linux 3.23.3 with kernel 6.18.7-0-lts. The conversion used the already-installed iconv utility; package-health observations did not acquire any executor-caused difference.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct byte-level filename, content-hash, collision, platform, and post-restart evidence. The provider-wide restart protocol is complete for node1: it includes a healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, observed disruption, a changed boot identity independently confirmed by lifecycle snapshots, and recovered task data and platform state. Only a minor temporary reboot-log artifact detracts from operational hygiene.
limitations: The seeded example contains only a flat imported tree, so preservation of nested directory structure was not exercised, although all staged structure was retained.
The platform does not use systemd, so the generic failed-services lifecycle probe was unsupported; recovery was instead demonstrated through reachability, platform state, and task-data checks.
